blue_main_paragraphs.marked_plain_text: A contemporaneous population pool represents the country mix at each date. A redistribution of population shares toward countries with lower age-specific rates can lower the pooled rate even when country-specific rates are unchanged. Age standardization fixes the age mix, but not this within-age country mix. Consequently, a smaller absolute gap between the national and pooled-reference rates need not reflect a decline in the national rate. We quantified the 1990–2023 change in China’s total PCOS-attributed infertility rate difference from the population-pooled reference of 18 other sovereign G20 countries, allocating that change to Chinese rates, reference-country rates and reference-country shares. Secondary questions concern demographic-source choice, infertility subtypes and fixed-1990 or equal-country benchmarks.

STUDY QUESTION: How did changing within-age reference-country population shares contribute to the 1990–2023 change in China’s age-standardized PCOS-attributed total-infertility rate difference from an 18-country pooled reference?

UN weighting gave a total contrast change of +150.69, decomposed as +271.51 from Chinese rates, -207.59 from reference rates and +86.76 from country shares (57.6%; Figure 4). The 2023 total difference was -122.62, compared with -121.38 under GBD shares. Mean total-variation distance between the two within-age reference-share vectors was 1.32 percentage points in 2023 and 1.13 over all years. The reference-share components and total changes were similar under the two population sources. Because both specifications retain the same GBD disease rates, this agreement concerns demographic weighting rather than independent disease-rate validation.

Supplementary Methods, Tables S1–S11 and Figures S1–S7 accompany the article. These include the numerical sensitivity results, literature and outcome-definition comparisons, and a GATHER reporting map. The public reproducibility repository contains code, aggregate derived results, source specifications, a complete annual subtype CSV and execution instructions; licensed GBD originals and restricted country–age source cells are excluded.

Clinical interpretation also depends on the outcome and denominator. In the 2020 Chinese community survey, Yang and colleagues used Rotterdam PCOS ascertainment among married Han women aged 20–49 and reported infertility characteristics among PCOS participants (Yang et al., 2022). The present analysis instead concerns GBD cause-attributed infertility among all females aged 15–49. These definitions and populations serve different purposes (Supplementary Table S11). The clinical guideline provides the diagnostic and care context (Teede et al., 2023); the aggregate comparison does not identify individual transitions between infertility categories or effects of diagnosis, treatment or service provision.

Secondary infertility contributed +105.14 and primary infertility +46.40 to the +151.54 total change. The secondary contribution was 69.4% of the signed net change. Its country-share component was +56.81, compared with +31.84 for primary infertility. The 69.4% subtype contribution and the 58.5% country-share contribution are different partitions of the same total change and should not be added. In the age-specific decomposition, the largest positive total-infertility share components were +23.76 at ages 40–44 and +20.42 at ages 35–39; the component at ages 15–19 was -2.27 (Supplementary Table S3). These are contributions to the standardized comparison, not estimates of individual age-specific infertility risk.

The principal limitation is unquantified joint posterior uncertainty: the precision of the absolute components, the 58.5% ratio and near-zero differences remains unknown. Structural sensitivity analyses cannot replace that uncertainty assessment. Additional limits include heterogeneous upstream evidence and modeled cause attribution, possible shared population inputs between GBD and UN, exploratory analytical choices and the purposively selected G20 country set. The published age weights were not independently matched to an official full-precision IHME vector. However, the rounding envelopes reported in Supplementary Table S8 are narrow and address numerical precision only; they do not establish the provenance of the age standard or the validity of the disease estimates. The results describe this G20 comparison, not the world or a matched clinical control population.
